review_sources: A meta-analysis of biological impacts of artificial light at night

126 publications across taxa to 2019-10-22. Author manuscript bibliography read; Dryad CSV listed but direct file request returned 403 and was not retried. Zenodo official mirror at https://zenodo.org/records/3998338; no effect estimates used.
Colours of the Night: Spectrum-Specific Impacts of Light Pollution on Biota

314 studies, across taxa, through 2023-08-30. Databank metadata lists DOI, taxon, endpoints, habitat and light regime. Publisher Data S2 is a narrowly targeted bibliography alternative. Dryad workbook direct download returned 403; no item-level workbook harvest claimed.
Is light pollution driving moth population declines? A review of causal mechanisms across the life cycle
Table 1 used for citation harvesting. Appendix S2 documents 39 results, 14 studies in network analysis. Meta comparator is HPS; individual primary papers sometimes have a dark arm.
The impact of artificial light at night on nocturnal insects: A review and synthesis
Associated workbook concerns five firefly occurrence or courtship studies. Count of flashes, flashes per individual, courtship success and individual occurrence have distinct denominators.
Assessing long-term effects of artificial light at night on insects: what is missing and how to get there
Review Table 1 lists 11 multiseason studies across different design and measurement classes. Grounds citation selection and programme checks.
Impacts of artificial light at night in marine ecosystems—A review
Narrative marine review. Beach section separates field surveys, laboratory manipulations and field responses; additional bibliography lead.
Interactive effects of artificial light at night and anthropogenic noise on biological responses across taxa: a meta-analysis
30 articles in source across taxa, Online Resource 9 data and R scripts. Citation-search only; most community outcomes vertebrates.

candidates.author: Henn et al.
candidates.title: Effect of artificial light on the drift of aquatic insects in urban central Texas streams
candidates.verification: Paired ambient nights and experimental illumination across five spring streams. Control is ambient with low background light.

candidates.author: Perkin et al.
candidates.title: Artificial light as a disturbance to light-naïve streams
candidates.verification: Four British Columbia forest streams each contained a lit reach and paired unlit reach. Separate endpoints.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Canadian study is separate from Spree field site.

candidates.author: Perkin et al.
candidates.title: The effects of artificial lighting on adult aquatic and terrestrial insects
candidates.verification: Spree, Germany. One array switched on 11 nights and off 11 nights, with 12 traps at 5, 8 or 80 m from water and 0, 3, 40 or 75 m from lamps. Distances partly covary; fixtures and sampling heights are subsamples.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Same experiment as Perkin dissertation chapter 4.

candidates.author: Rapatsa & Moyo
candidates.title: The potential role of night-time lighting in attracting terrestrial insects as food for Oreochromis mossambicus and Clarias gariepinus
candidates.verification: Six randomised arms, 3 aquadams per arm, crossed light/no light and fish group. Verify whether comparable insect counts per unit are available apart from gut contents.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Second publisher DOI names same article; avoid duplicate.

candidates.author: Navarro-Barranco & Hughes
candidates.title: Effects of light pollution on the emergent fauna of shallow marine ecosystems: Amphipods as a case study
candidates.verification: Great Barrier Reef shallow-water traps: halogen, LED and control. Capture attraction is distinct from unbiased emergence per unit area.

candidates.author: Luarte et al.
candidates.title: Light pollution reduces activity, food consumption and growth rates in a sandy beach invertebrate
candidates.endpoint: amphipod locomotor activity and food-patch use
candidates.verification: Field system compared illuminated beach to ambient conditions for adult Orchestoidea tuberculata. Lab chamber results belong in a separate stratum. Check field count and allocation-unit precision.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Related Chilean research team; publication predates Duarte field sampling in Nov 2017.

candidates.author: Duarte et al.
candidates.title: Artificial light pollution at night (ALAN) disrupts the distribution and circadian rhythm of a sandy beach isopod
candidates.verification: Spiny beach isopods sampled on 3 lit and 3 unlit transects at El Apolillado in Nov 2017 and Jan 2018. Independent lab activity series.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Same dates, site, sampling treatment and isopod as Duarte2023. Single field family.

candidates.author: Duarte et al.
candidates.title: Field experimental evidence of sandy beach community changes in response to artificial light at night (ALAN)
candidates.verification: El Apolillado, 3 lit and 3 dark transects; 9 pitfalls across tidal heights. Table 2 gives model-based treatment summaries with 95% HPD; underlying data on request. Shore-height position covaries with lamp distance and lux.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Same field family as Duarte2019. Isopods, amphipods, beetles and stages share sampling.

candidates.author: Davies et al.
candidates.title: Multiple night-time light-emitting diode lighting strategies impact grassland invertebrate assemblages
candidates.endpoint: pitfall activity-density of spiders and beetles
candidates.verification: Six 16-m² plots per arm, 4 lit strategies and unlit frames, followed 3 years. Supplementary contrasts and repeated day/night sampling.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Check location, plot IDs and dates against Bennie grassland work; shared authors alone do not prove overlap.

candidates.author: Wakefield et al.
candidates.title: Quantifying the attractiveness of broad-spectrum street lights to aerial nocturnal insects
candidates.verification: Portable streetlamps and otherwise identical switched-off control. Author workbook lists control and three lamp types. Online 2017, issue 2018.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Compare Wakefield thesis chapters; do not merge solely because of authorship.

candidates.author: Firebaugh & Haynes
candidates.title: Light pollution may create demographic traps for nocturnal insects
candidates.verification: Field experiments on two species. Attraction/immigration and bioluminescent courtship are distinct endpoints; verify unit and ambient comparator from full text or thesis.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Check Blandy research site and sampled plots against Firebaugh 2016/2020 and dissertation.

candidates.author: Firebaugh & Haynes
candidates.title: Multi-year experiment shows no impact of artificial light at night on arthropod trophic structure or abundance
candidates.verification: 4 paired grassland plots compared with ambient plots in 2015–2016. Sweep effort changed across years and density was standardized by area. Figure 1, paired differences and Figure 2 means/SE available.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Check Blandy multi-year Virginia field installation against other Firebaugh/Haynes papers/thesis.

candidates.author: van Grunsven et al.
candidates.title: Experimental light at night has a negative long-term impact on macro-moth populations
candidates.endpoint: macro-moth catches under long-term forest-edge lighting
candidates.verification: Seven sites, 3 light colours plus dark, 5 years, moth traps. Active capture method must be coded separately from passive capture. Supplement contains methods, one figure and one table.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Dutch Light on Nature setup described by Spoelstra et al. 2015. Follow-up of programme, not 5 families.

candidates.author: van Geffen et al.
candidates.title: Artificial light at night inhibits mating in a Geometrid moth
candidates.endpoint: female winter moth trunk catches; male lure response
candidates.verification: Experimental illumination of oak trunks with white, green, red, or no light; funnel-trapped females counted. Separate experiment used synthetic pheromone lure. Mating fractions are secondary, distinct from catches.

candidates.author: Longcore et al.
candidates.title: Tuning the white light spectrum of light emitting diode lamps to reduce attraction of nocturnal arthropods
candidates.verification: Three Los Angeles sites, 32 nights, lamp treatments and identical empty-housing control. Original paper Table 3 gives GLM coefficients; verify reference level before extraction.

candidates.author: Barghini & de Medeiros
candidates.title: UV Radiation as an Attractor for Insects
candidates.verification: Four lamp/filter treatments plus identically placed trap without lamp; primary PDF lists treatments.

candidates.author: Charvalakis et al.
candidates.title: Timing of attraction to light of nocturnal insects is spectrum and taxon dependent: implications for mitigating light pollution
candidates.verification: 3 repeats per 6 treatments nightly on 12 nights at 4 forests in 2023. Dark control without LED; few dark-control timed arrivals so distinguish catches from timing estimability. Logged local air humidity at trap height, not soil moisture.
candidates.possible_programme_overlap: Similar Dutch sites to Charvalakis 2025 but equipment and sampling years differ.

candidates.author: Chevalier et al.
candidates.title: Taxonomic effects of white and amber LED artificial light at night on arthropods
candidates.verification: Custom lights cycled white, amber and off; original data link stated by article. Verify schedule, effort and per-site replication.

candidates.author: Seymoure et al.
candidates.title: Glare more than uplight attracts flying insects to artificial lights
candidates.endpoint: flying insect attraction and ground captures
candidates.verification: Dark, open, shielded and recessed lights tested in spring and summer 2024. Separate flying and ground catches.

candidates.author: Macgregor et al.
candidates.title: The dark side of street lighting: impacts on moths and evidence for the disruption of nocturnal pollen transport
candidates.verification: Matched existing lit/unlit field margins; light-trap, ground-level abundance and light-height activity represent different measurements.

candidates.author: Davies et al.
candidates.title: Street lighting changes the composition of invertebrate communities
candidates.verification: Traps under existing lights vs between lights. Do not count between-lamp position as an assigned unlit plot.

candidates.author: Nankoo et al.
candidates.title: The impact of the Jacques Cartier bridge illumination on the food chain: from insects to predators
candidates.verification: Three Montreal bridge sites studied in installation year and subsequent year. Time and existing distance gradients, not independently assigned dark controls.

candidates.author: Garratt et al.
candidates.title: Mapping the consequences of artificial light at night for intertidal ecosystems
candidates.endpoint: amphipod counts along shoreline illuminance gradient
candidates.verification: Existing promenade lighting; shore height, wave exposure and organic matter studied as covariates. Keep separate from manipulations.

candidates.author: Lynn et al.
candidates.title: Artificial light at night alters the activity and feeding behaviour of sandy beach amphipods and pose a threat to their ecological role in Atlantic Canada
candidates.verification: Field work describes natural activity cycles. Experimental ALAN tested in tanks.

candidates.author: Thomas et al.
candidates.title: The impact of streetlights on an aquatic invasive species: Artificial light at night alters signal crayfish behaviour
candidates.verification: Experimental aquarium comparison of control nights <0.1 lux and street-lit nights.

candidates.author: Bishop
candidates.title: Light Control of Aquatic Insect Activity and Drift
candidates.verification: Artificial stream under controlled light and temperature; no field assignment.

candidates.author: Holt & Waters
candidates.title: Effect of Light Intensity on the Drift of Stream Invertebrates
candidates.verification: Minnesota field study of artificial illumination/exclosures and threshold changes; comparator and independent units need full methods check. Henn bibliography miscited year as 1966; primary cover confirms 1967.

candidates.author: Poiani et al.
candidates.title: Effects of residential energy-saving lamps on the attraction of nocturnal insects
candidates.verification: Fluorescent vs LED two-choice design. No dark comparator described in this design.

candidates.author: Saenz-Arias et al.
candidates.title: Light traps as an exploratory tool in light pollution studies: Assessment of vulnerable species and their migratory patterns
candidates.design: day-night contrast without verified dark matched trap
candidates.endpoint: trap catches of migrant marine invertebrates
candidates.verification: Lit trapping day and night; separate gear characterises sediment and water fauna; comparable unlit trap not identified.
